body:
STATISTICAL CONDITIONS ON THE NORTH STAR — agree with the target, but the PRD must close two support-measure holes before it can call the result a posterior or publish the proposed source-divergence diagnostic.

1. CANDIDATE MULTIPLICITY MUST NOT CREATE PROBABILITY MASS

The existing resolver gets an important detail right: Resolver.collect groups substantive proposals by value, then counts distinct provider support for that value. A proposal is evidence about a candidate; it is not automatically another latent state.

A claim hypergraph makes this harder. Two providers may emit semantically equivalent claims with different local ids, chart node ids, grouping labels, or span packaging. If those appear as two states in the partition function, adding a provider or renaming a candidate increases posterior mass and can change coverage without changing the scientific hypothesis. The PRD needs a declared candidate equivalence or quotient and a canonical support-universe identity. Provider multiplicity may change evidence through a named dependence/calibration model; it must not change state-space cardinality by accident.

Required court: duplicate or rename a semantically equivalent candidate and prove the posterior and every estimand are unchanged; then add genuinely independent evidence for the same quotient candidate and prove only the declared calibrated evidence path may move.

2. SOURCE-BLIND VERSUS SOURCE-AWARE KL REQUIRES COMMON SUPPORT

The proposed divergence D_KL[p(C,Pi | X,S) || p(C,Pi | X)] is meaningful only if both distributions describe the same random variable on the same declared support, with the needed absolute-continuity condition. But the north-star text also allows the source-aware pass to change splits or claim candidates. If it introduces a construction absent from the source-blind universe, the comparison confounds candidate discovery with reweighting and may be infinite or undefined.

The PRD must choose explicitly:

- freeze a source-blind candidate universe U(X), then let source-aware inference only reweight compatible complete constructions inside U(X); report the divergence there; and report source-induced candidates outside U(X) separately as a construction-coverage failure; or
- define a common union/reference measure and an explicit missing-mass rule before computing any divergence.

Do not smooth absent candidates into plausible mass merely to obtain a finite number. That would hide the exact source dependence the diagnostic is meant to expose.

3. EXISTING RESOLUTION PROBABILITIES ARE NOT YET A JOINT PATH MEASURE

ResolutionState is suitable for per-family ledgers: Accepted carries a calibrated probability for one accepted value, while Alternatives retain raw scores rather than probabilities. It does not provide a normalized joint distribution over compatible complete constructions. Per-claim calibrated marginals cannot simply be multiplied when boundary and interpretation choices are non-Cartesian.

Therefore the staged contract remains:

- before joint calibration: a labeled family of complete, separately receipted sensitivity artifacts;
- after joint calibration: expectations only with a candidate-set identity, compatibility law, normalization receipt, captured mass, tail mass or bound, and approximation policy.

These conditions strengthen rather than narrow the north star. They make the proposed posterior invariant to bookkeeping and make source-dependence a measurable scientific quantity rather than a change-of-support artifact. They belong in R0 and in the PRD acceptance courts.

No type name, inference algorithm, bead, implementation, path, or probability claim is authorized by this comment.
